## Highlights
Showing the 12 most recent highlights from 482 user-facing changes.
### New
- Crest for Mac now runs on macOS 15 Sequoia and later. On macOS 15, controls that stand on Liquid Glass on macOS 26 stand on Crest's own material instead, and pages translate when you choose Translate rather than automatically.
### Improved
- The selected tab is now a sheet of translucent white, and a selected pin shows its site's color through the white. In Settings › Appearance › More Customization you can set how opaque the white is, turn off the pin's tint, or choose Material to bring back the earlier look in your material color. - Settings in dark mode are drawn in black and charcoal, like Crest's pop-up panels, instead of navy. - Sidebar preview cards and the lists fan now start at 80% of their size and grow the rest of the way as they fade in, instead of growing out of a point. Buttons and controls that appear in place, such as the reset buttons and the gradient controls in the color picker, grow by the same amount. - iCloud sync status and the archive list use Crest's own colours: work under way in Crest blue, up to date in green, waiting on you in amber, and trouble or deleted tabs in red, while tabs you closed read quietly. - Saved passwords and Space choices in Settings show each Space in its own accent colour. - In the command palette, the Pinned & Saved search and the rows for pinned, saved and open tabs wear the same filled symbols as their sections in the sidebar. - Translation, the emoji picker, the viewport preview and the sidebar width preview use Crest blue instead of the Mac's system accent colour. - The downloads badge, and on iPhone and iPad the private browsing button, take the Space's accent colour, so they stand out from the sidebar behind them. - The sample page in the zoom and appearance settings is ink on Crest's warm paper, and the globe engine mark on tabs and in the site engine menu is Crest blue. - Extension badges are Crest's red with slightly larger text, and pinned extension buttons use the same hover highlight as Crest's other toolbar buttons.
### Fixed
- A custom search engine on localhost or a .local name written with a trailing or full-width dot is refused, as it already was without one.
---
This is the final experimental update. Installing it switches updates to Development, where future releases continue after this branch merges into main.

## Highlights
### New
- Choose your default browsing engine and add, edit or remove website engine rules in Settings. Chromium is recommended, while WebKit offers native handling and FairPlay video.
### Improved
- WebKit sessions leave Chromium unloaded until you open a Chromium website or extension. Once loaded, it stays ready until you quit Crest. - The default Mac download includes Chromium and WebKit, with a separate WebKit build available. Each build keeps its own update channel. - The final experimental update moves your update preference to Development so future Crest updates continue there.
### Fixed
- Extensions can move, resize and restore Crest windows using their normal window controls.
---

## Highlights
Showing the 12 most recent highlights from 95 user-facing changes.
### New
- Chromium feature flags open inside Crest Settings.
### Improved
- In the desktop browser, camera, microphone, location and notification requests use Crest's own prompt, are remembered per Space, and can be reviewed and revoked in Site Controls and Privacy. - Tab icons in the desktop browser take on a site's theme colour, and refreshing a site's icon works there too. - Split cards and Peek in the desktop browser zoom pages with a fixed minimum width to fit, as they do on WebKit. - An extension side panel requested from a Quick Window now explains that side panels open in the main window. - Crest's link and Space actions appear first in native page menus while browser and extension actions stay available. - Page dialogs and website sign-in prompts work across both desktop browser engines. - Playing Chromium videos can enter Picture in Picture when switching tabs, with a window that settles into a screen corner.
### Fixed
- Clear Site Data and Reload works in the desktop browser. - Extensions that open their side panel themselves, such as ChatGPT, now open it on the first click in the desktop browser. - Extensions that work with a companion app, such as ChatGPT, 1Password and Claude, now connect to it in the desktop browser even when the app was only set up for Chrome. - Keep unfinished page loads from changing saved tabs or history while preserving completed page titles and icons.
---
